selected.rationale: The Sustainability Buyer has a core category affinity for sustainable apparel and actively researches supply chains, making them a direct match for a brand made from recycled ocean plastic with sustainability as its primary value.
The Fitness Enthusiast focuses heavily on performance apparel and technical fabrics, fitting the activewear category and pricing tier of the brand.

The Wellness Optimizer has a low price sensitivity and affinity for fitness, aligning with the premium positioning between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective and responding well to science-backed or material transparency claims.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes convenience and meal kits, and explicitly dislikes luxury positioning, whereas the brand is a premium-tier one-off purchase.
The Gen Z Aesthete has a typical AOV of $48, which is far too low for a brand positioned between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective with an estimated AOV of $100.
The Pet Parent focuses strictly on pet food, supplies, and health rather than women's activewear.
The Affluent Classic prefers classic apparel, home goods, and travel with a messaging focus on heritage and craftsmanship, which does not fit a modern sustainable activewear brand.
The Convenience-First Millennial focuses on instant delivery and subscription services, whereas the advertiser is a one-off apparel purchase brand.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has high price sensitivity and looks for discount-forward messaging, conflicting with the premium price tier of the brand.
The Gifter is disinterested in self-care-only framing and relies heavily on holiday timing or gifting presentation rather than core activewear buying behavior.
